skill.name: inngest
skill.description: Design Inngest background jobs, event-driven workflows, scheduled functions, and durable execution patterns for serverless applications.
skill.summary: Build reliable Inngest workflows with durable steps, retries, concurrency controls, scheduling, and idempotency.

content.value_statement: Background jobs often fail across retries, delays, and service boundaries. This skill guides durable Inngest workflows with reliable steps, events, and controls.
actual_capabilities: Design typed Inngest clients and event schemas.
Create durable functions with named steps, sleeps, and retries.
Apply concurrency limits and idempotency to critical workflows.
Model fan-out, scheduled jobs, webhooks, and long-running pipelines.
Configure Next.js serve handlers and function registration.
Review workflows against practical Inngest validation checks.
limitations: It does not deploy applications or provision Inngest accounts.
Examples require adaptation for your framework, SDK version, and data services.
It does not replace testing against the Inngest development server.
External services such as Stripe, Resend, and databases need separate configuration.

use_cases.title: Launch a background job
use_cases.description: Create a typed Inngest function and serve route for a new serverless application.

use_cases.title: Harden payment processing
use_cases.description: Add durable steps, retries, idempotency, and concurrency controls to payment workflows.

use_cases.title: Design an AI pipeline
use_cases.description: Split long document processing into durable, rate-limited steps with stored results.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter function
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Inngest function for [event] in [framework]. Include typed event data, one durable step, and the required serve handler.

prompt_templates.title: Add a scheduled workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Inngest cron function that runs [schedule], processes [records], limits concurrency, and emits child events for independent work.

prompt_templates.title: Make a webhook durable
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my [provider] webhook into an Inngest workflow with signature validation assumptions, idempotency, retries, named steps, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a production pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-stage Inngest pipeline for [workload]. Specify events, step boundaries, fan-out, concurrency keys, retry policies, timeouts, and observability points.

output_examples.input: Design a welcome email sequence after user signup.
output: Trigger on a typed user signup event.
Load the user in a durable step.
Send the welcome message, sleep for 24 hours, then send onboarding tips.
Limit concurrency to protect the email provider.

output_examples.input: Review an order workflow for duplicate charges.
output_examples.output: Use the order identifier as an idempotency key. Isolate payment in a named step and configure bounded retries and concurrency.

output: Separate extraction, chunking, embedding, and storage into durable steps.
Apply a concurrency limit for the embedding provider.
Store stable vector identifiers derived from the document and chunk.

best_practices: Use stable, descriptive identifiers for every function and step.
Set idempotency and concurrency controls around payments and limited services.
Use typed events, bounded retries, and explicit timeouts for maintainable workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not place an entire workflow inside one large step.
Do not call payment services without a stable idempotency key.
Do not create unbounded fan-out against rate-limited dependencies.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Next.js, Express, Hono, Remix, and SvelteKit patterns, with the most complete route example for Next.js.

faq.question: Can it create scheduled jobs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design cron-triggered functions, child events, concurrency limits, and failure handling.

faq.question: Does it support webhook processing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers event ingestion, durable processing, idempotency, retries, and provider-specific integration boundaries.

faq.question: Can it deploy my workflow?
faq.answer: No. It can prepare integration code and deployment guidance, but account setup and deployment remain external tasks.

faq.question: How does it reduce duplicate work?
faq.answer: It recommends stable function identifiers, event-based idempotency keys, and durable step boundaries.

faq.question: Does it replace local testing?
faq.answer: No. Validate generated workflows with your tests, the Inngest development server, and current SDK documentation.
